adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — `GET /groups/:name/members` response changed from a bare JSON array to `{members:, meta:}` and the default page size dropped from 200 (automatic only) or unbounded (non-automatic) to 50, which breaks any existing API/plugin caller that expects an array or the full member list (P1, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifies the finding: `GroupsController#members` changed from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, and it now enforces pagination for all groups with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` (previously only automatic groups were limited, defaulting to 200, and non-automatic groups returned the full list). This is an intentional API shape/semantics change to support pagination (front-end updated to read `result.members` / `meta`), but it is a backward-incompatible contract change for any existing callers expecting an array or unpaginated results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:18 — `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, so when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 of 50) it reports one page too many; `showingLast` stays false and "next" moves to an empty page with offset == user_count (P2, conf 100)

For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — `limit`/`offset` come straight from params with no clamping (`(params[:limit] || 50).to_i`), so `limit=0` makes the client divide by zero in currentPage/totalPages, a negative value raises a SQL error, and a very large limit brings back the unbounded query this change was meant to remove (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used directly in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. From the diff, the client (`Discourse.Group#findMembers`) trusts `result.meta.limit/offset` and sets them onto the model, and admin UI computes `currentPage/totalPages` by dividing by `limit`, so `limit=0` from the server would break pagination math. Also, negative/very large values can defeat pagination (e.g., `LIMIT -1` in Postgres effectively removes the limit, and very large limits can be used to pull huge result sets), and negative offsets can trigger DB errors. This is a real, diff-grounded correctness/perf issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — `create` no longer reads `alias_level` even though the client's `asJSON` sends it, so any alias level chosen when creating a group is silently dropped and the group saves with the default (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the client now sends `alias_level` when creating a group: `Group.asJSON()` includes `alias_level` and `create()` POSTs `data: this.asJSON()` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js). However, the new server-side `Admin::GroupsController#create` only sets `name` and `visible` (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb) and never assigns `group.alias_level` from `params[:alias_level]`. As a result, any alias level chosen in the UI during group creation will be ignored and the group will persist with the model default.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:647 — `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` with an integer id instead of a User record, so it goes around the `group.remove` path that `add_members` uses via `group.add`; the add and remove paths become asymmetric and the removal may not take effect or update user_count (P2, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show an asymmetric implementation: `add_members` iterates usernames and calls `group.add(user)`, while `remove_member` does `group.users.delete(user_id)` (with an integer) rather than a symmetric `group.remove(user)` call. This could bypass any logic/callbacks encapsulated in `Group#remove`, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it’s broken: there’s a new spec exercising `remove_member` that expects the member count to drop to 0, and nothing in the diff shows a required callback/user_count update that `delete(id)` would miss. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group_member.hbs:1 — `{{#unless automatic}}` resolves against the group-member view/member context, not the group, so the remove "x" is rendered for automatic-group members too (sibling flag `automatic` not propagated to the member item; server returns 422) (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/templates/group.hbs` members are rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, which creates a `group-member` view per item. The new view (`admin/views/group-member.js.es6`) does not define/receive an `automatic` property, yet `admin/templates/group_member.hbs` gates the remove link with `{{#unless automatic}} ... {{/unless}}`. In this item view context, `automatic` will resolve to the view (or member) context, not the group/controller’s `automatic`, so it will be falsy and the "remove" link will render even for automatic groups. Server-side `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` rejects automatic groups with 422, matching the reported broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — `create` sets only name and visible and ignores `params[:alias_level]` even though asJSON (group.js:314) sends it, so the alias level chosen on a new group is silently dropped (sibling flag not propagated) (P2, conf 75)
